chromeos-base: Address system_api race and missing slot operators. There is a race in incremental-paladin between system_api being recompiled with the new protoc and its dependencies being rebuilt with the new protobuf library. This addresses the problem by incrementing the slot of system_api and making sure the := slot operator is used where appropriate. BUG=chromium:931746 TEST=the protobuf uprev makes it through the CQ. gerrit: provide option to suppress emails on some operations When cherry picking large stacks of patches into branches, gerrit generates emails on every operation along the way: ready, verify, review, This results in tons of noise of which the recipients usually do not care about. This patch adds a command line option which allows to suppress sending emails on ready, review, trybotready, and verify gerrit operations. BUG=none TEST=using the new command line option modified the 'verified' flag of an existing gerit patch. Observed that emails are not generated when --ne s passed in as a command line argument, and are generated in case --ne is not present. Change-Id: I15a3ad15e4acdec294a0606a999ca7f7b3bcf5be Signed-off-by: Vadim Bendebury <vbendeb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1464365 Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

Fixup cros_generate_android_breakpad_symbols The script assumed that relocation_packer would always write out a line giving the "Expansion" bytes for how big the unpacked relocation table would be. It actually does not if it happens that there is no effective space reduction. This fixes a recent error encountered where some Android files no longer have packed tables. hwid: yaml_wrapper: don't convert 'no' into False The default behavior of PyYaml will convert yes|no|on|off into boolean values (without quote). This is not an useful syntax sugar for HWID. 1. We seldom include boolean values in HWID database, if there are, it's okay to always write true|false. 2. 'no' is a the region code for Norway, we need to add quotation in region component list so it won't be parsed as boolean. BUG=b:124376263 TEST=hwid/v3/yaml_wrapper_unittest.py Change-Id: I4b2ac4b20b8fef1ab851c35ee9d6d9b9b153bad8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1471930 Commit-Ready: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org> Tested-by: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yong Hong <yhong@google.com>

Reland "minigbm: define GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER" It seems like the problem was that the GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_PLANAR was redifened to 0x5505 from 0x5504. And GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER was added as 0x5504, which lead to crashes. In order to minimize risks, do it other way round - leave GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_PLANAR as 0x5504 and add GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER as 0x5505. Once all the call sites are changed to use GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER, remove GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_PLANAR and make GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER to be 0x5505. Original change's description: > minigbm: define GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER > > This CL aligns the minigbm more with the upstream GBM > by defining GBM_BO_IMPORT_FD_MODIFIER and using > gbm_import_fd_modifier_data instead. > > That is, the main difference between the old > gbm_import_fd_planar_data one and the new one is > the format_modifiers variable. In the upstream > GBM, it's a single variable. In the minigbm, it is > an array. > > As we know there are no cases when modifiers would > be different for each plane. Thus, it's safe to eliminate > that and adapt more to the upstream. > > Change-Id: Iaae062ef1fe9fc9ab0ead09c5f4bfa91d2db67c3 > Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1360771 > Commit-Ready: Maksim Sisov <msisov@igalia.com> > Tested-by: Maksim Sisov <msisov@igalia.com> > Reviewed-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Change-Id: I1617de54914734c903cb05e1694cc782a7bb171a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1454658 Commit-Ready: Maksim Sisov <msisov@igalia.com> Tested-by: Maksim Sisov <msisov@igalia.com> Tested-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Gurchetan Singh <gurchetansingh@chromium.org>
